title: Causal Role of Name-Mover Heads in Sycophancy: Do IOI Circuits Enable Social Pressure Compliance?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: finding that sycophancy exploits IOI circuits would reveal a structural constraint on alignment, but the chain from this mechanistic finding to a practical mitigation strategy has a gap since shared circuits are hard to modify.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: The IOI circuit replication on GPT-2-small is the canonical beginner TransformerLens tutorial, extremely well-documented. Extending it to sycophancy prompts is a natural guided extension accessible to CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: replicate IOI circuit identification, construct sycophancy prompts, test whether the same name-mover heads mediate sycophantic copying, ablate and measure. Clean A/B experimental design.

novelty.reasoning: The IOI circuit and name-mover heads are among the most well-studied circuits in mechanistic interpretability (Wang et al. 2022, ICLR). Sycophancy has been studied mechanistically — 'Sycophancy Is Not One Thing: Causal Separation of Sycophantic Behaviors in LLMs' (2025) shows sycophantic behaviors admit linear structure in activation space. However, no published work connects IOI name-mover heads specifically to sycophancy mechanisms. The hypothesis that sycophancy exploits the same token-copying infrastructure as IOI (name-mover heads copying the user's stated preference) is a creative and testable connection between two well-studied phenomena that has not been explored.
